**What this research is about**

We are trying to identify the parents of Patrick Flynn, a man born around 1845 who lived and died in Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania. His death in 1908 is documented, and we want to establish who his father and mother were — moving from a documented fact to a proven family relationship.

**The story so far**

Records from two different decades place Patrick Flynn in the same Schuylkill County household — the household of a man named Thomas Flynn. In the 1850 census, Patrick appears as a five-year-old living with Thomas Flynn, who was then about 32 years old. Ten years later, in the 1860 census, Patrick is there again, now 15, still in Thomas Flynn's household. The 1850 and 1860 census takers recorded this at the time of their visits, making these contemporaneous observations. Neither census, however, explicitly states who was whose father — the relationship column did not appear on federal census forms until 1880 — so the father-son relationship is inferred from household position and shared surname, not directly stated.

Patrick's 1908 death certificate goes one step further: it names "Thomas Flynn" as Patrick's father. However, the man who provided this information was Patrick's son-in-law, James Brown — someone who was not present at Patrick's birth and was reporting what he had been told. That still counts as evidence, but it carries less weight than a firsthand account.

Taken together, the evidence strongly suggests that Thomas Flynn of Schuylkill County was Patrick Flynn's father. Three separate records from three different times all point in the same direction, and no record has turned up suggesting a different father.

Two things remain unresolved:

First, a birthplace contradiction: the two census records say Patrick was born in Ireland, but his death certificate says Pennsylvania. Second, an identity question: two Patrick Flynns of similar age (one age 5, one age 6) were living in different Schuylkill County households in 1850. A probate search is currently underway — we are looking for Thomas Flynn's will or estate records from roughly 1870 to 1890. If Thomas Flynn's will names Patrick as his son, that would be a powerful and independent confirmation of the relationship, and would go a long way toward resolving both open questions.
